contract.direct_answer:
The smallest validating Morpheus step ("prueba pequeño") is to build a single-field 1D (or thin 2D strip) reaction-diffusion model of ONE morphogen on a small fixed lattice, and check that it reproduces the expected steady-state gradient shape before any cell behavior, multiple fields, or coupling is added. Concretely, in the RN13 Morpheus .xml (the niche that holds simulation models + code):

1. Define ONE Field (the morphogen concentration) on a small Lattice — a 1D line or a short 2D rectangle, coarse resolution, no CellTypes/CPM yet.
2. Add a localized Source at one boundary (constant production or a fixed Dirichlet boundary condition) and a linear Degradation term, plus a Diffusion coefficient — i.e., the minimal production–diffusion–decay system (∂c/∂t = D∇²c − k·c + source).
3. Run to steady state and verify the analytic expectation: an exponential decay profile with characteristic length λ = √(D/k). That single check — does the gradient reach the predicted steady-state exponential with the right length scale and is it numerically stable (no oscillation/negative values, insensitive to lattice/timestep refinement) — is the validating unit test.

Only after this single-morphogen field validates against λ = √(D/k) do you scale up to multi-field / multi-cell coupled models. Kinetic parameters (D, k, source) would come from RN3 (signaling networks and kinetic parameters), and any geometry/mechanics from RN6, but the retrieved bundle does not contain a specific worked morphogen example, so the exact parameter values must be sourced there.</parameter>
